title: I and you: -mi and -si; my name is ...

video.title: मम परिचयः संस्कृत में
video.focus: Listen for मम नाम ... (my name is ...) and how each self-introduction sentence is built.

recap: Your Day 14 quiz answers didn't come in, so start with this warm-up. W1: Say 'He writes' in Sanskrit. W2: Which is right: सा पठती or सा पठति? W3: Fill in कः or का: ___ वदति? सा वदति।
idea: Yesterday every verb ended in **-ति** (he/she reads). Today you talk about **yourself** and **the person in front of you**.

Grammar sorts speakers into three **persons** (पुरुष): **1st person** = the speaker (I), **2nd person** = the one spoken to (you), **3rd person** = anyone else (he, she, it). Careful: Sanskrit grammar books name them the other way round: उत्तम पुरुष = I, मध्यम पुरुष = you, प्रथम पुरुष = he/she.
- अहम् ahám → **-आमि**: पठामि paṭhāmi - I read
- त्वम् tvam → **-सि**: पठसि paṭhasi - you read
- सः / सा → **-ति**: पठति paṭhati - he/she reads
Notice the **long ā** before -मि: पठ + मि becomes पठामि, not पठमि. So गच्छामि, लिखामि, वदामि, खादामि.
**Hindi trap:** Hindi needs हूँ / हो (मैं पढ़ता हूँ, तुम पढ़ते हो) and changes for male/female. Sanskrit needs neither: पठामि alone means 'I read / I am reading', for a man or a woman.
Because the ending already shows the person, अहम् and त्वम् can be dropped: पठामि। = I read.
**मम नाम रमेशः।** = My name is Ramesh. No word for 'is' is needed. **तव नाम किम्?** = What is your name?
Before a consonant, the final म् is written as anusvara (Day 2): अहम् → अहं पठामि, त्वम् → त्वं लिखसि.
The video may add अस्मि ('am') or अस्ति ('is'). Both are correct; Sanskrit just often leaves them out. For strangers and elders, spoken Sanskrit prefers the polite भवान्/भवती (Day 32).

quiz.why: अहम् (I) takes -आमि: लिखामि. -ति is for he/she, -सि for you.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: त्वं ___। (You read.)

quiz.why: तव = your; मम = my; त्वम् = you.

quiz.q: Translate into Sanskrit: My name is Gita.
quiz.why: मम (my) + नाम (name) + गीता. No word for 'is' is needed.

quiz.q: गच्छामि on its own (with no अहम्) means:
quiz.why: The ending -आमि already says 'I', so अहम् can be left out.
